Bassist Larry Ridley was born in Indianapolis, Indiana on September 3, 1937.

He played with Freddie Hubbard and Wes Montgomery as a teenager and went on to perform and record with many prominent jazz artists. Larry recently retired as professor from Rutgers University and is currently the head of the IAJE African American Jazz Caucus.
Larry was interviewed in Toronto, Canada on January 10, 2003 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Toronto at the IAJE convention. I’m extremely pleased to have Larry Ridley with me today.

You have had a marvelous career in different parts of the music. And I’m wondering if when you were a boy or a young man at what point did you set your career path? Is it possible — was it that definite of a time?
